title: High Levels of IgG Antibodies to the Spike Antigen of SARS-CoV-2 Among Health Care Workers in Kosovo
content:
Introduction: From 12 March 2000, when the first cases of COVID-19 were registered in Kosovo, to 9 March 2023, there were a total of 273,310 reported cases of COVID-19 and 3,211 reported deaths in Kosovo (CFR: 1.17%). Health care workers (HCWs) have been at a higher risk of contracting COVID-19 infection; nevertheless, data on seroprevalence of SARS-CoV-2 antibodies among HCWs in Kosovo are very limited. 
Methodology: A cross-sectional serology study with 1,654 healthcare professionals throughout of Kosovo was conducted to determine the presence of antibodies to the spike antigen of SARS-CoV-2. In addition, a structured questionnaire was administered to study participants to obtain basic demographic data and information on prior infection and COVID-19 vaccination status. 
Results: Antibodies to the spike antigen of SARS-CoV-2 were detected in almost all (99.8%) HCWs that participated in the study.  The average antibody titer was 8,347 AU/ml in women and 9,533.7 AU/ml in men. Sixty-four per cent of HCWs in this study reported prior COVID-19 infection, 6% of whom were hospitalised. Over 98% of study participants had received SARS-CoV-2 vaccination. 
Conclusions: Almost all HCWs participating in the study had antibodies against the spike antigen of SARS-CoV-2. This is most likely the result of the high COVID-19 vaccination rate in Kosovo, as well as COVID-19 infection.
